## Goal
ROADMAP 3.5 describes the monthly toast as "3 new removals confirmed, 1 relisted, handled". `progress_counts` and `progress_body` (`notify.py:67-84`) only know sent, confirmed and need-you. Add a `relisted` count: the number of distinct brokers whose status went `REMOVED -> REAPPEARED` since the window started, read from the recent events (`store.events(limit=2000)`, newest first, `to_state == REAPPEARED`, `ts >= since`, `broker_id` not starting with `_`). When it is zero the toast text is exactly what it is today; when it is positive one clause is added ("1 site put a listing back; we are on it"). Counts only; no names.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Fake store with events: two brokers REAPPEARED inside the window (one twice), one before it, one with a reserved `_checklist` id: `relisted == 2`.
2. `progress_body` with `relisted == 0` returns the same string as before for the same other counts (existing test strings unchanged).
3. With `relisted == 1` and `== 2` the clause is singular and plural; wording avoids "erase", "guarantee", "100%"; reading level check on the whole body (average sentence length under 18 words).
4. The toast is still not sent when nothing was sent, confirmed or relisted, and IS sent when only `relisted > 0` (this changes the quiet rule on purpose; test both).
5. The event read is bounded; a store error while reading yields `relisted == 0` and never raises.
6. Existing notify tests pass unchanged except where the quiet rule above is intentionally extended (say which in VENDOR_STATUS.md; do not edit tests outside your paths: the extension must not break `tests/test_notify_monthly.py`).

**Limits (every Grok WO, CLAUDE-G-004):** offline only. No network, credentials, git or gh, installs, or running the real app against real sites or a real mailbox; never read anything outside the repo. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Tests pass on Windows too (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`). Check `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and the in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard.
